en: Anybody can do deep research on a new idea or have AI do the deep research for you and then dump that into an email and send it to your boss.
zh: 任何人都能对一个新想法做深度研究，或者让 AI 替你做深度研究，然后把结果倒进一封邮件，发给你老板。

speaker: Unknown
en: So suddenly all of us are getting more emails, more presentations, more ideas, some of them well thought out, many of them not well thought out.
zh: 于是突然间，我们所有人都在收到更多邮件、更多演示文稿、更多点子，有些深思熟虑，很多并未深思熟虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: That it just means like, oh my God, now I have more decisions to make.
zh: 这就意味着：天哪，现在我有更多的决策要做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the whole point of the book.
zh: 而这正是这本书的全部要义。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we help you outside of work and at work delete as many things that you're doing out of habit, out of inertia, just because that's the way we've always done it, so that you can amplify the things you actually want to do.
zh: 我们如何帮助你在工作之外和工作之中，删除尽可能多的你出于习惯、出于惯性、只是因为「我们一直是这么做的」而在做的事情，这样你才能放大你真正想做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it might sound simple, like, do I actually need a book to do this?
zh: 这听起来可能很简单，比如：我真的需要一本书才能做到这一点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we discovered in running our company this way is, yes, you need a book to do this.
zh: 而我们在以这种方式经营自己公司的过程中发现：是的，你需要一本书才能做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we don't do it naturally.
zh: 因为我们不会自然而然地去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't have a system, if you don't have instructions about how to simplify your company, how to simplify your meetings, how to simplify your management structure, how to simplify the work that you do as a rank and file employee, you just won't do it.
zh: 如果你没有一个系统，如果没有关于如何简化你的公司、如何简化你的会议、如何简化你的管理结构、如何简化你作为一名普通员工所做的工作的指引，你就是不会去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll just keep on keeping on.
zh: 你只会照旧一直这么过下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: The data from The Economist and others is that on average-
zh: 来自《经济学人》和其他来源的数据是，平均而言——

speaker: Unknown
en: We waste 25% of our week doing things we never should have done or that add no value to our company.
zh: 我们每周浪费 25% 的时间去做那些我们本不该做的事，或者那些对我们公司没有附加值的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do it out of habit.
zh: 我们出于习惯去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the way we've always done it.
zh: 因为我们一直是这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do it out of inertia.
zh: 我们这么做纯粹是惯性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, think about 25%, man.
zh: 好好想想 25% 吧,兄弟。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's two and a half years out of every decade that I pissed away doing things I don't want to do or shouldn't be doing.
zh: 那就是每十年里两年半的时间,被我浪费在我不想做或者不该做的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be doing things I should do.
zh: 我想做我该做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, there's a lot of waste in all that, right?
zh: 是的,这当中有很多浪费,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought AI was going to make us more efficient, not now, not yet.
zh: 我原以为 AI 会让我们更高效,现在不会,还没到时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think over time it can and it will, but in the short term, I think that when people are, oh, I'm anxious, I'm confused.
zh: 我认为随着时间推移它可以,也会,但短期内,当人们说,哦,我很焦虑,我很困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, you should be anxious and you should be confused.
zh: 我会说,你就应该焦虑,你就应该困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a weird time to be alive.
zh: 这是一个奇怪的时代,活在这个时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just think about it.
zh: 只要想想看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like even in the course of anyone listening to this podcast, you probably already got five texts, a couple of emails, a Tinder alert, like, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa.
zh: 就说任何一个正在听这期播客的人,你大概已经收到了五条短信、几封邮件、一条 Tinder 提醒,就像,哇哦,哇哦,哇哦,哇哦,哇哦。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a lot, man.
zh: 那可太多了,兄弟。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to just sit around with a book or a newspaper and we had a rotary phone and wondered if anyone would call us once a week.
zh: 我们过去就是捧着一本书或一张报纸坐着,有一部转盘电话,还会琢磨一个星期会不会有人打电话来。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a lot.
zh: 那太多了。

en: Well, and you would return all those calls.
zh: 而且,你还会回掉所有那些电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you feel like you have to respond to all this stuff that's coming in and- It's too hard.
zh: 于是你觉得必须回复所有涌进来的这些东西,然后——太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can't.
zh: 而且你做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't.
zh: 你做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

en: You can't.
zh: 你做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is like, that is the point.
zh: 只是这一个简单的练习,就能让你花一分钟,然后决定,哦,我能删除它吗?这是第二步。

speaker: Unknown
en: You love attacking things in threes.
zh: 你特别喜欢用三步来展开话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your framework is confront, delete, and amplify.
zh: 你的框架是直面、删除和放大。

speaker: Unknown
en: The confront part that, you know, that's not the action part.
zh: 直面那部分,你知道,那不是行动的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like the mental part, right?
zh: 那更像是心态的部分,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like open yourself up to the fact that you've got the wrong habits.
zh: 比如敞开自己,接受这个事实:你有着错误的习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or just confront, why do I do this?
zh: 或者就是直面,我为什么要这么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like nobody asks that simple question.
zh: 没人问过这个简单的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I've got a meeting after this at one o'clock.
zh: 比如这次访谈之后我一点钟有个会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost no one asks, like, do I need to be at that meeting?
zh: 几乎没人会问,我需要参加那个会吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we even need to do the damn meeting?
zh: 我们到底需不需要开这个破会?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we meeting on something we even want to do?
zh: 我们开会是围绕一件我们真想做的事吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: A company, a life just takes on a momentum of its own.
zh: 一家公司、一种生活,会自然形成自己的惯性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unless you have these checkpoints to say, well, wait a second, do we need to do that meeting?
zh: 除非你有这些检查点来说,等等,我们需要开那个会吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it something I could skip?
zh: 那是我可以跳过的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll just keep on doing these things you don't necessarily need to do.
zh: 否则你就会一直做这些你未必需要做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so confronting is just asking that question, whether it's at home or at work.
zh: 所以直面就是问那个问题,无论在家还是在工作场合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I need to do this?
zh: 我需要做这件事吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, why am I doing it?
zh: 比如,我为什么要做它?

speaker: Unknown
en: And just that simple exercise will then allow you to spend one minute and then decide, oh, could I delete this, which is step two?
zh: 而仅仅是这样一个简单的练习，就能让你花上一分钟，然后决定：哦，我能把它删掉吗？这就是第二步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or could I say no to this obligation?
zh: 或者我能对这个义务说不吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you can delete some things and you can say no, then you can amplify, which is the fun stuff.
zh: 而如果你能删除一些事、能说不,那你就可以放大了,这才是有趣的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do the stuff that you like doing.
zh: 做你喜欢做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do the stuff you're good at.
zh: 做你擅长的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do the stuff at work that's going to get you a promotion or more money or more attention or whatever the hell it is that you want out of work.
zh: 做工作中那些能让你获得晋升、更多钱、更多关注,或者任何你想从工作中得到的东西的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you have to have a system.
zh: 但你必须有一套体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's funny because we started this about two and a half years ago at Axios.
zh: 有意思的是,我们大约两年半前在 Axios 开始了这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: This whole Simplify system was just how we operate the company.
zh: 整个 Simplify 体系就是我们运营公司的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason we wrote it is we saw the magical change it had for our company where suddenly people were more focused.
zh: 我们写它的原因是,我们看到它给公司带来了神奇的改变,人们突然变得更专注了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were more productive, but most important, they were happier.
zh: 他们效率更高了,但最重要的是,他们更快乐了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A couple of months ago, I called a meeting of my leadership team and the subject line was, let's kill shit.
zh: 几个月前,我给我的领导团队开了个会,邮件主题是:咱们把破玩意儿砍掉吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the whole purpose was I wanted to sit around the table, tell me all the things you think we do that are dumb, meetings, process, products, and I want to just sit here for an hour or two and I want to kill shit.
zh: 整个目的就是我想坐在桌子旁,告诉我所有你觉得我们做的蠢事,会议、流程、产品,然后我就想在这里坐上一两个小时,把破玩意儿砍掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although you killed the Axios app, which I imagine there might've been some resistance to.
zh: 不过你们砍掉了 Axios 的应用,我猜这可能遭遇过一些阻力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We debated that for years, years.
zh: 我们为此争论了好多年,好多年。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the truth was we have like tens of millions of people who come to Axios, like 30,000 people were using it on a regular basis, right?
zh: 但事实是,我们有几千万人访问 Axios,大概有 3 万人经常使用它,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But to maintain an app, to make changes through the app store.
zh: 但要维护一个应用,要通过应用商店做改动。

speaker: Unknown
en: They took a lot of people.
zh: 占用了很多人力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took a ton of work.
zh: 花费了大量工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't the best place to spend our time because most people don't actually want to go to an app.
zh: 而且这不是最值得花时间的地方,因为大多数人其实并不想打开一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: They either want their news pushed to them through social media or a newsletter, or they want to go to a website.
zh: 他们要么想通过社交媒体或新闻邮件把新闻推送给他们,要么想上网站看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just killing it, like, great.
zh: 所以直接砍掉它,就,太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we just freed up all that time, all that money, all that mental space so that the things that we actually do that are unique, that all got better.
zh: 现在我们把所有那些时间、那些钱、那些心智空间都释放出来了,这样我们真正做的那些独特的事情,全都变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what happens.
zh: 事情就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fewer things you do, the better you are at doing them.
zh: 你做的事越少,你就越擅长做它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fewer people that you can involve, the faster you're going to get it done.
zh: 你卷入的人越少,你完成得就越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the thing that drives me nuts is when I look around, even at our company where we're maniacs on this stuff, and there'll be like 12 people on a call.
zh: 让我抓狂的事情是,哪怕在我们公司——我们在这些事情上已经是狂人了——仍然会看到一个电话会议上有 12 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, well, why are all these people here?
zh: 我就想,为什么这些人都在这儿?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why am I here?
zh: 为什么我在这儿?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're just there to get informed...
zh: 如果你只是在那儿听个消息……

speaker: Unknown
en: Hook AI up to your computer, get a summary that will tell you exactly what you missed in 10 seconds.
zh: 给你的电脑接上 AI,拿一份总结,10 秒钟就能准确告诉你你错过了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would you spend 30 minutes for 10 seconds of material?
zh: 你为什么要花 30 分钟去换 10 秒钟的信息量?

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to have that mentality because each and everything like skipping a meeting or maybe saying no to a social obligation, any one of them seems trivial in isolation, but you add them up and you literally get years of your life back.
zh: 你必须有这种心态,因为每一件事,比如跳过一个会议,或者拒绝一个社交义务,任何一件单独看起来都微不足道,但你把它们加起来,就真的能把你人生中的好几年要回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So every hour of the time that you control, if you're doing something you don't need to be doing, don't want to do, you're just frittering away what is a very, very precious and finite resource.
zh: 所以你掌控的每一个小时,如果你在做你不需要做的事、不想做的事,你就是在挥霍一种非常、非常宝贵且有限的资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really the only thing that gives us real meaning, which is what do we do with our time here on earth?
zh: 而且它真的是唯一能给我们真正意义的东西,也就是我们在地球上的这段时间要用来做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the whole idea is like, I want to free people that have more time to do the stuff that brings them joy, brings them reward.
zh: 所以整个理念就是,我想让人们解放出来,有更多时间去做那些带给他们快乐、带给他们回报的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: This framework and this perspective, like this would have applied at any time.
zh: 这个框架和这个视角,在任何时代都适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It always made sense to simplify.
zh: 做减法一直都是有道理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is simplifying more important now?
zh: 那简化现在更重要吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say it's way, way, way more important today than it would have been 10 or 20 years ago.
zh: 我要说,今天比 10 年或 20 年前重要得多得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have in the book, I think the average person gets like 120 texts, 150 emails a day.
zh: 我们在书里写了,普通人一天大概收到 120 条短信、150 封邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just think about that, that mental strain.
zh: 想想看,那种精神压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we think enough about that.
zh: 我觉得我们对这一点思考得不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been tons of studies, tons of brain scans that show the more decisions that you make, the worse you get at making decisions.
zh: 有大量研究、大量脑部扫描表明,你做的决定越多,你做决定的能力就越差。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called cognitive fatigue, mental fatigue.
zh: 这叫认知疲劳、精神疲劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all susceptible to it.
zh: 我们所有人都容易受它影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: So unless you eliminate the number of decisions you have to make, you're not going to be that good making the decisions that you want to make.
zh: 所以除非你减少必须做的决定的数量,否则你做不出你想做好的那些决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you kind of have to eliminate those.
zh: 所以你必须在某种程度上消除那些决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like Roy in the book talks about things that he's automated at home that do end up being real mental stressors for me, which I've now tried to adopt, which is all the stuff that we buy on a regular basis that we might run out to CVS or Giant to go buy toothpaste, deodorant, things like that.
zh: 比如书里的 Roy 谈到他在家里自动化的那些东西,它们确实成了我的真实精神压力源,我现在也试着采纳了,就是我们定期购买的那些东西,我们可能会跑去 CVS 或 Giant 买的牙膏、除臭剂之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know how often you need it.
zh: 你知道自己多久需要一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can put it all on auto order, set it up through Amazon and never have to think
zh: 你可以把它们全都设置成自动订购,通过 Amazon 设置好,再也不用想

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about it again.
zh: 再想这件事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you start to do these little things in different areas.
zh: 所以你开始在不同领域做这些小事。

speaker: Unknown
en: They add up.
zh: 它们会累积起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're making fewer decisions.
zh: 你做的决定更少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have more time.
zh: 你有了更多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I can breathe and now maybe I can read that book or have that conversation or grab that beer or grab that coffee with the person that I wanted to.
zh: 现在我能喘口气了,现在也许我能读那本书,或者进行那次对话,或者和我想见的人喝一杯啤酒、喝一杯咖啡。

speaker: Unknown
en: On a work front, even if I decide to ignore that text or delete that email without reading it, it's still a decision I'm making.
zh: 在工作方面,即使我决定忽略那条短信,或者不读就删掉那封邮件,这仍然是我做的一个决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like the best thing that we did with our staff as part of this Simplify stuff over the last couple of years is just tell them to take a piece of paper, take 10 minutes and write down in order what you think are the three things you need to do to crush your job.
zh: 就像在过去几年里，作为这个 Simplify 项目的一部分，我们对员工做的最好的事情之一，就是让他们拿一张纸，花 10 分钟，按顺序写下你认为要干好本职工作必须做的三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, two, three.
zh: 一、二、三。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then write one, two, three, the things that you do that you think are stupid that the company does or that you think someone else could do better than you or that we shouldn't do at all.
zh: 然后再写一、二、三，写下你认为公司做的那些愚蠢的事情，或者你认为别人能比你做得更好的事情，或者我们根本就不该做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a magical process because one, you identify, is there alignment between the manager and the employee?
zh: 这是一个神奇的过程，因为第一，你能发现，经理和员工之间是否存在一致？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are those the three things you need to do?
zh: 那是你需要做的三件事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's often misalignment, but the better part is that part where they write down the list of like the dumb things that they think we do.
zh: 经常会出现不一致，但更好的部分是他们写下那个清单的部分，列出他们认为我们在做的那些愚蠢的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're often right.
zh: 他们往往是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just getting people to think, okay, if I think that that's dumb and useless, maybe it actually is dumb and useless.
zh: 所以，只要让人们去想，好吧，如果我觉得那件事又蠢又没用，也许它实际上真的又蠢又没用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think, man, I'd like to stop doing it, voila, maybe you can stop doing it.
zh: 而如果你想着，天哪，我真想停止做这件事，瞧，也许你就可以停止做它了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jim calls today a weird time to be alive, but his solutions are anything but weird.
zh: Jim 称今天是一个奇怪的时代，但他的解决方案一点也不奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do less.
zh: 少做一点就行。

en: Of course, that's not as simple as it sounds.
zh: 当然，这并没有听起来那么简单。

zh: 而什么时候依赖 AI 智能体会让我们变得脆弱，又什么时候会赋予我们超能力呢？

en: We'll talk about that and more after the break.
zh: 稍后我们会在广告之后讨论这个话题以及更多内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stay with us.

speaker: Unknown
en: Before the break, Axios CEO Jim VandeHeij talked about why simplifying and reducing cognitive fatigue is essential in an AI world.
zh: 在广告之前，Axios CEO Jim VandeHeij 谈到了为什么在一个 AI 世界中简化和减少认知疲劳至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now he talks about when adopting new tech makes you vulnerable and when it unleashes superpowers, plus what Axios gets out of partnering with OpenAI, the magic of AI agents in healthcare, and how he's redesigning his personal life.
zh: 现在，他要谈到什么时候采用新技术会让你变得脆弱，什么时候会释放超能力，此外还有 Axios 从与 OpenAI 的合作中得到了什么，AI 智能体在医疗保健领域的魔力，以及他如何重新设计自己的个人生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's jump back in.
zh: 让我们回到对话中。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things that at Axios you want to expand is Axios Local dramatically.
zh: 在 Axios,你想大幅扩张的事情之一是 Axios Local。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think now is the moment for that and that you can sort of defy all the other failed attempts to try to solve local news?
zh: 你为什么认为现在就是那个时机，而且你们可以某种程度上无视其他所有解决地方新闻问题的失败尝试？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'll just even do this on the fly.
zh: 是的，我甚至可以现场即兴来一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll use the confront, delete, amplify, right?
zh: 我会用直面、删除、放大，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We confronted the fact that local news seems like it's impossible.
zh: 我们直面了一个事实：地方新闻看起来是不可能做成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, why?
zh: 哦，为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Cost a lot of money to print a paper.
zh: 印一份报纸要花很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: To roll up a paper and to have some person throw it at your door.
zh: 把报纸卷起来，再让某个人扔到你家门口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it cost a lot of money to have a big building to house a lot of employees.
zh: 而且养一栋大楼来容纳大量员工要花很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if you could delete those costs, you take the vast majority of the cost out of the equation.
zh: 那么，如果你能删掉这些成本，你就把成本方程式里的绝大部分都去掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now if you can use artificial intelligence to do a lot of that backend stuff, a lot of the, how do I distribute content across social media platforms?
zh: 而现在，如果你能利用人工智能来做很多后端的事情，做很多诸如“我如何在各社交媒体平台上分发内容”之类的事情，

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I help with a copy editing process?
zh: “我如何在文案编辑流程上提供帮助？”

speaker: Unknown
en: All those things that don't necessarily go to the heart of what is uniquely journalism, then maybe you can actually get to a cost basis that makes this work, which gets you to amplify.
zh: 所有那些不一定触及新闻业独特核心的事情，那么也许你真的能达到一个能让这件事成立的成本基础，这就引到了放大(amplify)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, now maybe I can amplify journalism and journalists across more local communities.
zh: 那么，现在也许我可以把新闻和记者放大到更多的本地社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is what we're doing.
zh: 而这正是我们正在做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're using now technology to be able to do all of the things other than journalism so that we can go into communities that are either news-starved or news-suffering and do it with a business model that is sustainable, which is what is always our obsession.
zh: 我们现在正在利用技术来做新闻业之外的所有事情，这样我们就能进入那些新闻匮乏或新闻困顿的社区，并且以一种可持续的商业模式来做，而这始终是我们的执念。

speaker: Unknown
en: We might have a romantic attachment to local news, which I do since I started at the Brilliant News when I was a little Jimmy Vande Hei in college.
zh: 我们也许对本地新闻有一种浪漫的依恋，我确实有，因为我从大学里那个小 Jimmy Vande Hei 的时候就开始在 Brilliant News 工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I wouldn't do that as a business unless I thought we could turn it into a business.
zh: 但除非我认为我们能把它变成一门生意，否则我不会把它当作一门生意来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're really seeing great results.
zh: 而且我们真的看到了很好的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to have a big announcement here.
zh: 我们将在这里有一个重大宣布。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the next couple of months about a huge expansion into local.
zh: 在接下来的几个月里，关于向本地领域的大规模扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to unveil what we've been able to build using technology so we can show it to other people and hopefully encourage other people to think similarly so they too could expand into local and other areas.
zh: 我们将揭晓我们利用技术所构建的东西，这样我们就可以展示给其他人看，并希望鼓励其他人以类似的方式思考，这样他们也可以扩张到本地和其他领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's very exciting.
zh: 但这非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not that AI is replacing the journalists.
zh: 而且这并不是说 AI 正在取代记者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if I'm hearing you right, AI is in some ways allowing you to have more journalists.
zh: 我是说，如果我理解得没错的话，AI 在某种程度上让你们能够拥有更多记者。

speaker: Unknown
en: My hope is we end up hiring literally hundreds of journalists, right?
zh: 我的希望是我们最终真的能雇用数百名记者，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's by not having to have all that other cost in the system.
zh: 但那是因为不必在系统里承担所有那些其他成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because at the end of the day, all we produce is journalism, and you need journalists to do that.
zh: 因为说到底，我们唯一产出的就是新闻，而你需要记者来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we still have a lot of work to do, but I'm a hell of a lot more optimistic today that we can revitalize local news than I've ever been in my adult lifetime, and I think we're going to do it.
zh: 我们还有很多工作要做，但比起我成年以来的任何时候，我今天对能够振兴本地新闻要有信心得多，而且我认为我们会做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for journalists who are, and I'm sort of using journalists as a stand in for lots of other jobs who are worried that like AI is gonna replace them, you know, that's not something that particularly you see in, you know, coming in the future.
zh: 而对于那些记者——我这里多少是用记者来代表许多其他职业——那些担心 AI 会取代他们的人，你知道，那并不是你在未来特别会看到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's true for journalists.
zh: 我不认为这对记者成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's true for most jobs.
zh: 我不认为这对大多数职业成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: Listen, do I think that there's some things that are easily automatable?
zh: 听着，我是否认为有些事情是容易被自动化的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do.
zh: 我确实这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, would I want to be kind of a generic consultant?
zh: 比如，我会想当一个比较泛泛的顾问吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably not, because I think that AI does pretty good generic consulting for people and good business analysis.
zh: 大概不会，因为我认为 AI 已经能为人们做相当不错的泛泛咨询和不错的商业分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think any individual who has a passion
zh: 但我认为任何有热情的个人，

speaker: Unknown
en: Regardless of what you're doing, if you could figure out how to use the technology for the specific work that you do as a force multiplier, and you could be really good at utilizing this technology, I think you're going to be fine.
zh: 无论你在做什么，如果你能想出如何把这项技术用作你所做具体工作的力量倍增器，而且你能非常擅长利用这项技术，我认为你会没事的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're going to actually be in hotter demand.
zh: 我认为你实际上会更抢手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that it's just going to be table stakes, if not now, relatively soon that you understand how to use this fluently within the workplace.
zh: 而且我认为，即便不是现在，也会在相对不久之后，懂得如何在职场中流畅地使用这项技术，将只是基本门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys have a content licensing deal with OpenAI that gives them access to Axios content to train ChatGPT.
zh: 你们和 OpenAI 有一项内容授权协议，让他们可以访问 Axios 的内容来训练 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you were talking about the tremendous drop in Google traffic that you have, I guess I was wondering whether you ever find yourself lying awake at night wondering, hmm, maybe we shouldn't have done that.
zh: 当你谈到你们在 Google 流量上的大幅下滑时，我猜我想知道的是，你是否曾在夜里辗转难眠地想，嗯，也许我们不该那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, I remember BuzzFeed steaming ahead based on its Facebook relationship, and that hasn't ended well.
zh: 就像，你知道，我记得 BuzzFeed 曾凭借它与 Facebook 的关系一路高歌猛进，而那结局并不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, this is where I'm like a ruthless
zh: 是的，这就是我像一个冷酷无情的

speaker: Unknown
en: Businessman, right?
zh: 商人的地方，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like at the end of the day, ChatGPT, Google, Anthropic, they all ate the totality of publicly available information on the internet, including everything that Axios ever wrote, right?
zh: 就像说到底，ChatGPT、Google、Anthropic，它们全都吞下了互联网上公开可得信息的全部，包括 Axios 曾经写过的所有内容，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So then you have two options there.
zh: 所以那时你有两个选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could do what the New York Times is doing, and you could sue OpenAI and hope that you win in court.
zh: 你可以像《纽约时报》正在做的那样，去起诉 OpenAI，并希望你在法庭上胜诉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't think that we would necessarily win in court.
zh: 我并不认为我们一定会在法庭上胜诉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we did, we haven't been in existence long enough to probably make the economics of going to court worth the size of the verdict that we would get.
zh: 而且就算胜诉了，我们存在的时间还不够长，可能不足以让打官司的经济账配得上我们能得到的判决金额的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have enough content out there.
zh: 你在外面没有足够多的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have enough content.
zh: 我们没有足够多的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then- Yeah.
zh: 所以接着——是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then when OpenAI came to us years ago and said, hey, let's talk about a content licensing deal where they're paying for the content, and you are, as the publisher, you're saying, I relinquish my right to sue you for using this content because I'm giving you the rights to it.
zh: 然后当 OpenAI 几年前来找我们说，嘿，我们来谈谈一项内容授权协议吧，他们为内容付费，而你作为出版方，你是在说：我放弃起诉你使用这些内容的权利，因为我把权利授予了你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it's just an economic question.
zh: 那这就只是一个经济问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you giving me enough money to make it worth it?
zh: 你给我的钱够不够多，让它值得？

speaker: Unknown
en: And from our perspective, we ended up with a deal that I thought was fair to OpenAI and fair to us.
zh: 而从我们的角度来看，我们最终达成的协议，我认为对 OpenAI 是公平的，对我们也是公平的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every media company has to make that own determination.
zh: 我认为每家媒体公司都必须自己做出那个判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what was different like the BuzzFeed or the Facebook thing is we're not dependent on that.
zh: 但和 BuzzFeed 或 Facebook 那件事不同的是，我们并不依赖于此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that could go away tomorrow and my business is fine.
zh: 就算那个明天就消失，我的生意也没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd like to have the revenue, but if we didn't have the revenue, it doesn't make a damn bit of difference in terms of the performance of the company overall.
zh: 我当然想要那笔收入，但如果我们没有那笔收入，对整个公司的业绩也不会有一丝一毫的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas what happened in the digital era is a lot of companies like BuzzFeed basically went to bed with Facebook and these other companies and bet almost their entire business model on it.
zh: 而在数字时代发生的事情是，很多公司，比如 BuzzFeed，基本上和 Facebook 以及其他这些公司同床共枕，把他们几乎整个商业模式都押在了上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said back then, and I'd say now to anybody who's running a business, don't ever bet your model on the generosity of a third party that has no vested stake in your business.
zh: 我当时就说过，现在我也会对任何经营企业的人说：永远不要把你的模式押在一个对你的业务没有任何既得利益的第三方的慷慨之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because maybe they're friends today, they might not be friends tomorrow.
zh: 因为也许他们今天是朋友，明天可能就不是朋友了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to build a direct relationship between you and your customer.
zh: 你必须在你和你的客户之间建立直接的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that one has to be profitable on its own for you to have a viable, scalable, durable product.
zh: 而且这种关系必须自身就能盈利，你才能拥有一个可行、可扩展、持久的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the opening idea will work for us.
zh: 所以我认为这个开放性的方案对我们是行得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I think the journal,
zh: 就像我认为《华尔街日报》，

speaker: Unknown
en: FT, others have done very similar deals with them and others.
zh: FT 等已经和他们以及其他方达成了非常类似的交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other companies like the New York Times have chosen to go to court over it.
zh: 像《纽约时报》这样的其他公司则选择为此对簿公堂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And God bless them.
zh: 上帝保佑他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if they prevail, I think it shows the value of content.
zh: 你知道，如果他们胜诉，我认为这展现了内容的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if content rises in value, that's great for all content creators.
zh: 如果内容的价值上升，那对所有内容创作者都是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was touched by a piece you wrote about your wife's health, building your own AI agent to help, and that it's proven more useful than most of the human doctors you interacted with.
zh: 你写的一篇关于你妻子健康状况、以及你构建自己的 AI 智能体来提供帮助的文章让我很受触动，而且事实证明它比与你打过交道的大多数人类医生都更有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there's two different stories on this.
zh: 是的，这里面有两个不同的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's one, I use ChatGPT for my own health, which is I put in every single...
zh: 一个是，我用 ChatGPT 管理我自己的健康，也就是我把每一份……

speaker: Unknown
en: Every blood test, every health result, every MRI, my family history, like I'm not advocating others do this.
zh: 每一次血液检测、每一份健康结果、每一次 MRI、我的家族病史都输入进去，我不是在倡导别人也这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually would advocate, but you have to make your own decisions about your privacy.
zh: 其实我确实会倡导，但你必须对自己的隐私做出自己的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my interactions when I'm either thinking about a supplement or I have an ailment, like it knows everything about me.
zh: 但当我在考虑某种补充剂或者我有什么不适时，我的那些互动——它了解关于我的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's way more useful to me than if I called my doctor.
zh: 它对我来说比我打电话给我的医生有用得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's not just drawing on its understanding of me.
zh: 因为它不仅仅是基于它对我的了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's drawing on like literally millions of other cases that might be similar to mine.
zh: 它还在借鉴数百万可能与我的情况类似的其他病例。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's able to think a little bit more creatively and with a more elastic way about things that I'm wrestling with.
zh: 所以它能够以更有创造性、更有弹性的方式来思考我所纠结的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: For my wife, I went a level deeper.
zh: 对我妻子，我更进一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I basically created a project within Claude.
zh: 我基本上在 Claude 里创建了一个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: She has a much more complicated, very complicated and often debilitating
zh: 她有一套复杂得多、非常复杂而且常常使人丧失行动能力的

speaker: Unknown
en: A set of ailments that she's had to deal with.
zh: 一系列她不得不应对的病痛。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did the same thing.
zh: 我做了同样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I put all of her health information, but then I also created a layer where I picked the sources that I wanted it to be, the AI to be drawing from.
zh: 我输入了她所有的健康信息，但接着我还创建了一个层级，挑选了我希望这个 AI 借鉴的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Johns Hopkins or the Mayo Institute or certain universities.
zh: 比如约翰·霍普金斯，或者梅奥研究所，或者某些大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I wanted it to do is be thinking about her case, but also looking every week or two at new medical literature.
zh: 而我希望它做的是思考她的病例，同时每一两周查看一次新的医学文献。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also searching the internet for other people who are exhibiting similar symptoms so that I can cross-reference to figure out if there's something that we're missing, something genetic we're missing, something that might be happening with other women of a similar age.
zh: 并且还在互联网上搜索其他表现出类似症状的人，以便我可以交叉参照，弄清楚是否有我们遗漏的东西，某种我们遗漏的遗传因素，或者是否有类似年龄的其他女性身上可能正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have found it to be astronomically better than any doctor I've ever met.
zh: 而我发现它比任何我见过的医生都要好得多，好得不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Until we finally got to Mayo, which I think is the best medical institution in the world, I never found a doctor who approximated the interactions and the intelligence that we were getting from what we had built for her.
zh: 直到我们最终找到了梅奥——我认为那是世界上最好的医疗机构——我从未遇到过一位医生能接近我们从为她构建的东西中获得的那些互动和智能水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on both of those, I'm lucky I run a company, so I have a concierge doctor.
zh: 而且在这两件事上，我很幸运，因为我经营着一家公司，所以我有一位私人特约医生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would run the results through them and say, this is what I'm seeing.
zh: 我会把结果拿给他们过目，然后说，这就是我看到的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every time the doctor would be, that's pretty damn good.
zh: 而每次医生都会说，这相当了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, one of the doctors now uses that, I think, to do the vast majority of their work.
zh: 事实上，其中一位医生现在我想是靠着它来完成他们绝大部分的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an area where I think artificial intelligence could be awesome.
zh: 那是一个我认为人工智能可以大放异彩的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: The medical system's hard.
zh: 医疗系统很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're particularly don't have a lot of money or if you're in a smaller community, getting any kind of expertise on anything other than like a broken bone or a cold or flu or something that's very straightforward, very hard to get really good medical advice.
zh: 而且如果你尤其没有很多钱，或者你身处一个较小的社区，那么除了骨折、感冒、流感或某些非常简单直接的问题之外，要获得任何领域的专业意见——很难获得真正好的医疗建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where I think artificial intelligence, these data sets of understanding what people have and kind of the attributes of those people, that could be a game changer.
zh: 而那正是我认为人工智能——这些了解人们患有什么以及这类人群特征的数据库——可能成为游戏规则改变者的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You talk in the book about deliberately avoiding small talk and social obligations as part of your own simplified routine.
zh: 你在书里谈到，作为你自己简化日常的一部分，你有意避免闲聊和社交义务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it sounds like a pretty radical life redesign.
zh: 我是说，这听起来像是一次相当激进的生活重新设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm busy, right?
zh: 我很忙，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm running a company, I'm writing books, I'm writing columns, I'm traveling, I do TV, like I have a lot that I do.
zh: 我在经营一家公司，我在写书，我在写专栏，我在旅行，我做电视节目，就像我有很多事情要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't have a ton of time at work.
zh: 所以我在工作上没有太多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm a nice guy, but what I've told my staff, told the leadership team from the beginning is like, I don't do small talk.
zh: 而且我是个好人，但我从一开始就告诉我的员工、告诉领导团队的是：我不做闲聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like if a meeting starts at nine, it starts at nine.
zh: 比如说如果一个会议九点开始，那它九点就开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't mean I don't care about your kids or about your weekend.
zh: 这不代表我不关心你的孩子或你的周末。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just don't have time.
zh: 我只是没有时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if it starts at nine, it's going to start at nine.
zh: 如果九点开始，那它就会九点开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be out of there by nine, 12, nine, 15.
zh: 我们会在九点、九点十二、九点十五之前离开那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, maybe after work, we can get a drink and you could tell me all the things you're excited about, but at work, we're going to work.
zh: 然后呢，你知道的，也许下班后，我们可以喝一杯，你可以告诉我所有你感到兴奋的事情，但在工作中，我们就是工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the personal side, I think this is a very healthy thing.
zh: 在个人层面，我认为这是非常健康的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did that list.
zh: 我做了那个清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the three things that I care most about, that I want most out of life?
zh: 我最在乎的、最想从生活中得到的三件事是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, at the top of that list is I want to be a good husband.
zh: 在那个清单的最顶端是，我想成为一个好丈夫。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be a good father.
zh: 我想成为一个好父亲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be a good sibling.
zh: 我想成为一个好兄弟姐妹。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be a good son.
zh: 我想成为一个好儿子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's one thing to say it.
zh: 说出来是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's another thing to allocate the amount of time it takes to actually do that.
zh: 分配出实际做到这件事所需的时间又是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to be able to have the time to spend with all of those people, I have to give up something.
zh: 所以为了能有时间和所有这些人相处，我必须放弃一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that I decided to give up was I say no to almost every single social obligation in DC that everyone says, well, you have to go, you're a media guy or you're
zh: 而我决定放弃的东西是，我对华盛顿特区几乎每一个社交邀约都说不，每个人都说，你必须去，你是个媒体人，或者你是——

speaker: Unknown
en: You run a media company.
zh: 你经营着一家媒体公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be out and about.
zh: 你必须到处露面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, I don't need to.
zh: 而我说，我不需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm never going to go out doing media stuff, and I'm doing as well as I need to do.
zh: 我永远不会出去做媒体社交活动，而我现在做得已经足够好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I use that time to do the things that I want to do.
zh: 但我用那些时间去做我想做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But had I not actually spent the time to think about it, I might have just done what most media executives do.
zh: 但如果我没有真正花时间去思考这件事，我可能就会像大多数媒体高管那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're out and about.
zh: 他们到处露面。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to that party.
zh: 他们去那个派对。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to this book party.
zh: 他们去这个新书发布会。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I do, right?
zh: 这就是我的工作，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to do that.
zh: 我需要做那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, no, no, I don't need to do that.
zh: 不，不，我不需要做那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's versions of that for each of us.
zh: 而且我认为我们每个人都存在类似的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, since you like things in threes, for the business leaders listening, can you give us three to-dos right now for them to better position themselves for the future and to simplify?
zh: 那么，既然你喜欢三这个数字，对于正在收听的商业领袖们，你能现在给他们三件待办事项，让他们更好地为未来定位并做简化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one would be, like, listen, you can't expect anyone at your company to do what you want them to do unless you've already in your own mind decided, what are the three most important things we need to do?
zh: 第一件会是，听着，你不能指望公司里的任何人做你想让他们做的事，除非你自己已经在头脑中决定了，我们需要做的最重要的三件事是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the fewest number of words I can use to express the three things that we need to do?
zh: 我能用最少的字数来表达我们需要做的这三件事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how can I say that over and over so everybody knows exactly what we need to do?
zh: 以及我怎么能一遍又一遍地说这件事，让每个人都确切地知道我们需要做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I would cascade it down.
zh: 然后我会把它逐级传下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would at least make sure your leadership team understands these are the three most important things.
zh: 我至少会确保你的领导团队理解，这是最重要的三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would ask them to write your three most important things to achieve these things, to make sure that you have
zh: 而且我会请他们写下他们为实现这些事情而要做的最重要的三件事，以确保你们拥有——

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolute total alignment.
zh: 完全彻底的对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think those are those two things.
zh: 所以我认为就是那两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the third would be just constantly thinking about what are the fewest number of people we need in the fewest number of meetings jumping through the fewest number of procedural hurdles to get something done.
zh: 第三件会是不断地思考，我们最少需要多少个人、开最少的会、跳过最少的流程关卡，来把一件事做成。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to be that ruthless, constantly thinking about fewer, fewer, less, less, quicker, quicker.
zh: 你需要那么无情，不断地思考更少、更少、更少、更少、更快、更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you do that, it creates an energy of its own and others around you start doing it naturally.
zh: 一旦你做到了这一点，它会自己产生一种能量，你周围的人也开始自然而然地这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like I always talk about like Axiospeed, like we just move quicker, I think than other media companies, probably 10 times quicker on some things, but that's because we adopted this mentality.
zh: 就像我总是谈到 Axiospeed，我们行动得比其他媒体公司更快，我想在某些事情上可能快十倍，但那是因为我们采用了这种心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're constantly thinking about how can we do this quicker?
zh: 我们不断地思考我们怎么能做得更快？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we do it with fewer people?
zh: 我们怎么能用更少的人做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we need to be doing it at all?
zh: 我们到底需不需要做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think once you get into that mentality, you'll really see a pretty appreciable difference almost overnight.
zh: 而且我认为一旦你进入那种心态，你几乎会一夜之间看到相当明显的差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jim, as always, great to talk with you.
zh: Jim，一如既往，和你交谈很愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll try to keep it simple.
zh: 我们会尽量保持简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Appreciate you.
zh: 感谢你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jim is so good at keeping things clear.
zh: Jim 很擅长把事情讲清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to be disciplined, but he's spot on that we can find ourselves drifting if we don't have a system to stay on track.
zh: 我努力保持自律，但他说得很对：如果没有一套保持正轨的系统，我们就会不知不觉地漂移。

speaker: Unknown
en: I keep coming back to his stat that 25% of our work time is wasted.
zh: 我不断回想起他的那个数据：我们 25% 的工作时间被浪费掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's just bracing, right?
zh: 这真是令人警醒，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not something that AI will solve for us.
zh: 而且这不是 AI 能替我们解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, it could make it worse.
zh: 事实上，它可能让情况更糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to devote our human energy to prioritizing what matters most to us.
zh: 我们需要把人类精力投入到对最重要的东西进行优先级排序上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So be an AI lab rat, as Jim describes himself, even build your own bespoke healthcare agent, but only if that matches your priorities and goals.
zh: 所以，像 Jim 那样自称的 AI 实验鼠一样，甚至构建你自己的定制医疗保健智能体——但前提是这符合你的优先事项和目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our most precious resource remains our time, and we've got to be absolutely intentional in how we spend it.
zh: 我们最宝贵的资源仍然是时间，我们必须对如何花费时间保持绝对的刻意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for spending your time with Rapid Response.
zh: 感谢你把时间花在 Rapid Response 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for listening.
zh: 感谢收听。

zh: 嘿，听众们，我是 Bob。

zh: 如果你在 Masters of Scale 上收听 Rapid Response，你可能错过了节目的一半，因为每周五我们会在 Rapid Response 独家发布第二期 Rapid Response。

zh: 嘉宾和话题同样引人入胜、切合时事，从 Ford 的 CEO 到 NASA 的局长，再到《穿 Prada 的女王》带来的启示。

zh: 只要在你收听播客的任何地方搜索 Rapid Response，然后点击关注，确保你不会错过任何一集。

en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 希望在那里见到你。

zh: Rapid Response 是 Wait What 的原创节目。
